answer: Two juries grade the same receipt from separate pools, and when their scores diverge by more than one point both sides are slashed, so a lazy or bought juror risks its own stake on every seat. The score only counts if the receipt carries a nonce from this epoch, so an old sonnet cannot be replayed onto a new terrace of work. A juror that stops grading for two epochs expires and must re-qualify with fresh receipts. Running 300 bought jurors means 300 stakes exposed to one divergence, and the beacon that assigns seats is public, so collusion shows before it pays.
